content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem now: the root cause was the monthly-spend-feature flag flipping on at 09:09, exposing a latent ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py:35 on the account page, with no deploy in the window. Argus couldn't mitigate because the flag provider showed zero recent changes, so no rollback was possible, and it escalated with a draft PR instead. I want to flag the tension in the logs around this.

I should also avoid restating the given impact figures as if I computed them, so I'll describe the impact qualitatively -- roughly a third of account page requests failing over an ongoing period -- rather than offering precise derived numbers.

Beyond that, I want to lay out my assumptions clearly: the flag toggle inferred solely from log evaluation counts (with no corroboration from provider history), no deploy detected in the lookback window, an unknown end time meaning the duration is a lower bound and recovery is unconfirmed, errors attributed only to the account page path, and background disconnect errors treated as baseline noise. For the executive summary, I'll refer to the affected area generically as customers' account pages rather than naming internal components.

assumptions: The flag flip at 09:09 is inferred from the service's own flag-evaluation log lines. The flag provider's change history was queried twice and reported zero recent flag changes, so the toggle was never confirmed at the source; either the provider's history is incomplete or the change was made by a path it does not record.

No deployment or config change appears in the 24-hour (and narrower 134- and 74-minute) change lookbacks. The conclusion that the faulty division shipped in an older release is an inference from that absence, not from any observed release record.
Impact is attributed entirely to the account page path, because every ZeroDivisionError log line names it. Whether other endpoints touch the same code was not checked.
The recurring ClientDisconnected errors are treated as normal pre-existing background noise, not part of this incident.
The incident had not recovered by the last minute of metrics read, so any duration or impact figure for it is a lower bound, not a measurement. Nothing here should be read as a final cost.
The draft pull request is a proposed fix that was never applied or verified in production; it has not been shown to resolve the failure.
No mitigation was attempted and nothing was changed and rolled back, so the system state at handoff is the same state that was failing.
input.executive_summary: Starting at 09:09 UTC on 24 September 2026, a newly switched-on feature on the shop's customer account page failed whenever it tried to display a monthly spending figure. Customers loading their account page saw errors instead; browsing and other parts of the shop were not implicated. Roughly a quarter to a bit over a third of account page requests were failing in each minute observed, against a near-clean baseline beforehand. The automated responder picked the incident up about five minutes after onset, identified the cause within seconds, but had no safe control available to turn the feature back off or undo a release, so it took no corrective action. Instead it opened a draft code change for a human to review and handed the incident to on-call engineers about seven minutes after it began. The service was still failing at the last minute of data available, so the outage lasted at least as long as that window and the true end time is not known from this record.
input.root_cause: At 09:09 the `monthly-spend-feature` flag went from off to on (the logs show a mid-minute ramp of 42 off / 158 on, then fully on at 09:10), which made a previously dormant code path reachable; that path divides by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:35 and raises ZeroDivisionError on account page requests, replacing the sparse ClientDisconnected baseline errors with a sustained band of ZeroDivisionErrors. No deploy or config change was recorded in the 24 hours before onset, so the toggle - not a release - is the proximate trigger; the defective division itself must have shipped in some earlier release outside the lookback window.
